meta.description: Anima 2B LoRA for a 16GB laptop GPU (RTX 5080 Laptop class) with a large system-RAM pool. Training math is IDENTICAL to anima_lora_background (the model author's recipe: rank 32, AdamW 2e-5, batch 1 + grad accum 4, LLM adapter frozen, Block-only targeting via ignore_if_contains) - only memory/IO behaviour differs, so checkpoints are interchangeable with the background/performance presets. Three deltas vs background: (1) cache_latents true ALONGSIDE cache_latents_to_disk, so latents are written once and then served from RAM instead of being re-read and deep-copied from disk every step - matters most on native Windows, where the dataloader is hardcoded to num_workers 0 and every disk read is serialized with GPU compute; needs a few GB of RAM for a typical dataset, which is what the 96GB pool is for. (2) Preview sampling at 768 instead of 1024: on the 5090 gate-C run, steady-state training was 9.9-10.7GB but the PEAK was 14.1GB during 1024x1024 sample generation (both figures include a ~2.6GB desktop baseline) - sampling, not the training loop, is what would put a 16GB card at risk. Raise back to 1024 if you have headroom to spare. (3) ui_db_poll_seconds 2 throttles the UI's per-step sqlite polling (4 blocking SELECTs + 1 write every step) to once every 2s; the only cost is that the UI's stop/save-now/sample-now buttons take up to 2s to be noticed. NOT measured on 16GB hardware - the 14.1GB peak above is a 32GB 5090 measurement (docs/profiles.md); if you OOM, drop resolution to [512, 768] before touching batch/accum, since changing those changes the recipe. Like the other Anima presets, the author's sigmoid_scale 1.3 timestep widening is not supported by upstream's Anima implementation.
